resources.string: Fictional marker on the mucus side
Marker on the air side: %1$s a.u.
Mucus-side amount = total marker × (chosen percentage ÷ 100). Air-side amount = total marker − mucus-side amount. Both amounts are in arbitrary units (a.u.).

High in the nasal cavity, mucus covers the surface of the olfactory epithelium. Bowman glands beneath the epithelium supply mucus to that surface. This exercise splits an imaginary, inert marker across that mucus–air boundary without changing its total. The chosen share is hypothetical. It does not describe a real substance, predict smell, or assess anyone’s sense of smell.
